page.layout: One printed page, right-hand page of the book. Top: running head line with page number at left and running title at centre; below it a two-line motto (left-aligned) with initials "I. L. G." right-aligned; a rule; a large centred heading "EPICEDION CARMEN" with a subtitle block of small capitals; then one verse stanza (italic, with large initial S); a stanza of verse continuing; a signature line "TH. BEZA." right; then "TH. BE-" at the foot right (catchword-like fragment). No marginal notes.

main_text.l: Non mihi longa fuit fatis obstantibus aetas:
Nec mea longus humi conteget offa sopor.
SI perfecta tibi vivo quaecunque fuerunt,

l.i: Et tellus quicquid, quicquid & æquor habet.
Mundi ex quo fulsit tempore prima dies.

main_text.l: Noluit hoc cui sunt humana negotia cura,

l.i: Sed simul & nobis cauit & ille tibi.

main_text.l: Námque tui melior fruitur pars altera cælo,

l.i: Illa tibi vero tanto congesta labore,
Scriptis salua manent condita cunctla tuis.

page.notes: The stanza text was read from a small, partly faded scan; words marked for doubt are not individually flagged, so readings such as "cunctla" (printed as shown, possibly "cuncta") and "mariqúe" may be printing variants. The subtitle block was set in small capitals and is given in mixed case with the large initial letters expanded only where clearly printed. The motto line is faint on the scan. The "TH. BE-" at the foot is a catchword-like fragment of the next page's signature.
